Nvidia earnings: what Wall Street expects from the chipmaker

Published 2026-10-07 09:15 UTC

Nvidia reports quarterly results after the bell on Wednesday, and Wall Street analysts expect another big jump in revenue as demand for artificial intelligence chips continues. The consensus forecast calls for revenue of about $58 billion, up roughly 60% from a year ago, with data center sales making up nearly 90% of the total.

Investors will be watching guidance most closely. Analysts expect Nvidia to forecast revenue above $63 billion for the current quarter, and any figure below that range could weigh on the stock, which has gained more than 40% this year. The company's gross margin is expected to stay near 75%, though some analysts worry that the costs of ramping up new chip generations could pressure profitability.

Supply remains a key question. Nvidia depends on a single contract manufacturer for its most advanced processors and on a small number of suppliers for high-bandwidth memory. Executives have said supply is improving, but customers including cloud providers and AI startups still report long waits for the newest systems.

Analysts will also listen for comments about export restrictions. Rules limiting sales of advanced chips to some countries have cut into Nvidia's international revenue, and the company has developed modified products to comply. Any new restrictions or approvals could change the outlook for the coming year.

Competition is another theme. Rival chipmakers and several large cloud companies are designing their own AI accelerators, hoping to reduce their dependence on Nvidia. So far, Nvidia has kept its lead thanks to its software ecosystem, which makes it easier for developers to train and run models on its hardware.

Options markets imply the stock could move about 7% in either direction after the report, a swing worth hundreds of billions of dollars in market value. Because Nvidia is one of the largest companies in the S&P 500, its results often move the broader market and shares of other semiconductor firms.
